newsitem.title: USA: DSP Communiciations sees lower margins, sales gain.
newsitem.headline: DSP Communiciations sees lower margins, sales gain.

text.p: DSP Communications Corp expects its gross margins to recede to about 42 percent, or three percentage points less than its margin so far this year, when the company easily topped its own target, its executives said on Thursday.

The maker of chip sets for wireless digital communications also expects sales to grow rapidly as more Japanese and U.S. consumers and businesses begin using pocket digital cellular telephones, said Nathan Hod, DSP's chief executive, at the Montgomery Securities technology conference.
DSP was among the first companies to make a cellular phone chipset based on a single digital signal processor.
DSP's sales have doubled or tripled year over year in most quarters until the most recent three-month period, when sales rose 82 percent.
The vast majority of its revenues come from Japan, which Montgomery Securities describes as the largest and fastest-growing market for digital wireless communications.

DPS is also starting to make inroads in the U.S. market as more personal communications services are launched in the United States. It supplies NEC Corp and a second undisclosed company with chip sets for PCS handsets sold in the United States. The U.S. PCS market is growing by more 40 percent a year, Hod said.

Hod said DSP had expected its gross margins to slip to 39 percent this year because its product is sold into consumer markets where prices traditionally fall over time. Instead, its gross margin rose to 45 percent in 1996 largely because its vendors cut their prices.
Still, he told the Montgomery Securities conference that DSP expected its gross margin to slip to 41 or 42 percent "going forward."
